title.en: Thorlakr of Skalholt: Iceland's Saint and His Relics
title.zh: 斯卡爾霍爾特的索爾拉克：冰島聖徒及其聖髑

region.zh: 冰島斯卡爾霍爾特與蒂克瓦貝爾

texts.period: Thorlaks saga (13th-14th c.); Jarteinabok Thorlaks (the miracle-book); translatio of relics 1198; canonized 1984

source.work: Thorlaks saga byskups; Jarteinabok Thorlaks (the miracles of Thorlakr); ed. Biskupa sogur, Islenzk Fornrit XV (2003)

texts.license: Public domain (older editions); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Thorlakr Thorhallsson (1133-1193), bishop of Skalholt, becomes Iceland's official saint: a bishop of discipline (the celibacy-clause, the tithe-law), whose cult was voted at the Althing in 1200 and whose relics were translated in 1198 to the church of his foster-home Thykkvabaer, where the miracle-book records cures. The record is the saga of a national saint: the Icelandic church's own hagiography, with the native miracle-cycle of the country's first canonized? - official cult.
summary.zh: 斯卡爾霍爾特主教索爾拉克·索爾哈爾松（1133-1193）成為冰島的官方聖徒：一位厲行戒律的主教（獨身條款、什一稅法），其崇拜於1200年在冰島議會上獲准，聖髑於1198年遷至其義母家鄉蒂克瓦貝爾教堂，當地的奇蹟書記錄了諸多痊癒之事。此記錄是一部民族聖徒傳：冰島教會自撰的聖徒文獻，附有該國最早的正式崇拜之鄉土奇蹟週期。

texts.canonical_translation: Biskupa sogur, Islenzk Fornrit XV, Reykjavik 2003; paraphrase

narrative.en:
The Thorlakr-saga is the Icelandic church's own hagiography, and its doctrine is national discipline. The bishop's career: educated in Paris and Lincoln, returned as bishop of Skalholt (1178), enforced the celibacy-clause and the tithe-law - the Icelandic church's institutional maturation is the saga's frame. The cult: after his death (1193), the Althing of 1200 voted the sanctification (the native cult's legal act), and the relics were translated in 1198 to Thykkvabaer, the church of his fostering, which became the cult-center.

The miracle-book (Jarteinabok) records the cures: the blind restored at the relics, the mad bound and freed, the drowned child restored, the sick healed at the church's vigils - the native miracle-cycle of the national cult, with the saga's clause-history of the church's control (the miracles investigated by the bishops). The record's cultural functions are the national-saint doctrine (Iceland's own cult, voted by the assembly) and the institutional-hagiography doctrine (the miracle-book as the church's audit of its saint's power).

In the atlas, the record anchors the national-saint family: each a church's home-grown cult; the Icelandic one is distinctive in the assembly-vote.

The cult's history is documented in its institutional acts: the Althing's vote of 1200 (the sanctification's legal form), the 1198 translatio of the relics to Thykkvabaer, and the miracle-book's audit of the cures (each miracle examined, dated, and witnessed - the medieval church's evidentiary standards applied to the Icelandic cult). And the record's national dimension is the saga's own: Thorlakr is Iceland's first native saint, canonized formally only in 1984 but venerated since the Althing's vote - the cult's eight-century continuity documented from the medieval books to the modern canonization. In the atlas's hagiographic corpus, the record is the native-cult case-study: the national saint whose authority is the assembly's vote rather than the pope's decree.

The bishop's reform-record completes the doctrine: the celibacy-clause and the tithe-law are the Icelandic church's institutional maturation, and the saga frames the sanctity in exactly those terms - the reform-bishop's discipline as the cult's charter. And the miracle-book's evidentiary form completes the record: each cure dated, witnessed and examined (the bishops' investigation-clause), the medieval church's audit-standards applied to the Icelandic cult - the hagiography as institution rather than legend. The record thus anchors the national-saint family: the assembly's vote as canonization, the relic-translation as cult-founding, and the miracle-book as the church's self-audit. And the record's comparative placement completes the corpus: the national-saint family (each church's home-grown cult) and the reform-bishop portrait (sanctity as discipline) meet in Thorlakr - the Icelandic cult distinctive in the assembly-vote and the eight-century continuity from the Althing's decision to the modern canonization.

Institutional-hagiography: the miracle-book as the church's audit of the cult
Reform-bishop portrait: the celibacy and tithe reforms as sanctity
Relic-translatio: the 1198 translation founding the cult-center

title.en: Jon Ogmundsson of Holar: The Bishop and the Writing-Spirits
title.zh: 霍拉的約恩·厄格蒙德松：主教與寫字鬼

texts.period: Jons saga helga (13th-14th c.); ed. Biskupa sogur; principal MSS of the saga

source.work: Jons saga helga (the two writing-spirits episode); ed. Biskupa sogur, Islenzk Fornrit XV (2003)

texts.license: Public domain (older editions); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: Bishop Jon Ogmundsson of Holar (1052-1121) is Iceland's holy bishop of the north; his saga's most famous episode is the exorcism of the two writing-spirits: at the episcopal seat, two invisible spirits take up their quarters 'in? - the? - church? - and? - write? - on? - the? - walls? - the? - 'letters? - 'their? - 'grievances? - 'I? - am? - 'tormented? - 'here? - and the bishop's remedy: a mass and the consecration? - the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - the record is the Icelandic church's ghost-story par excellence: the haunt as a legal grievance, resolved by liturgy.
summary.zh: 霍拉主教約恩·厄格蒙德松（1052-1121）是冰島北方教會的聖主教；其薩迦最著名的段落是對兩個「寫字鬼」的驅逐：在主教座堂中，兩個隱形鬼魂在牆上寫下自己的怨訴——「我在此受苦」。主教的 remedy 是一場彌撒與祝聖儀禮。此記錄是冰島教會最經典的鬼故事：鬧鬼被寫成法律怨訴，而化解之法是禮儀。

texts.canonical_translation: Biskupa sogur, Islenzk Fornrit XV, Reykjavik 2003; paraphrase

narrative.en:
The Jon-saga's writing-spirits episode is the Icelandic church's ghost-story par excellence. The haunt: at Holar, the episcopal seat, two invisible spirits 'took? - up? - their? - quarters? - in? - the? - church? - 'and? - 'wrote? - 'on? - the? - walls? - 'their? - 'grievances? - 'the? - 'letters? - 'visible? - 'to? - the? - household: 'I? - am? - 'tormented? - 'here? - the haunt as a written complaint - the spirits' grievances in legible form. The remedy: the bishop's mass, the consecration of the church's spaces, and the spirits' departure - the haunt resolved by liturgy; and the saga's reading: the spirits were the restless dead of the place, bound by the bishop's offices - the conversion-era's dead accepting the new jurisdiction.

The record's cultural functions are the liturgical-exorcism doctrine and the grievance-haunt doctrine: the ghost's complaint is written - a legal document in spirit-ink - and the remedy is the church's own jurisdiction. In the atlas, the record anchors the church-ghost family: each a haunt resolved by the church's offices; the Holar one is distinctive in the writing.

The bishop's career frames the episode: Jon Ogmundsson studied abroad, reformed the northern see's discipline, and - the saga's miracles - exercised the exorcist's office across his diocese, the ghosts of the farms bound by his mass. And the writing-spirits episode's doctrinal point is the saga's own: the haunt's complaint is legible - the spirits write, and the writing is evidence - so the exorcism is a legal proceeding as much as a rite: the grievance read, the jurisdiction claimed, the departure enforced. The record thus completes the Icelandic church's ghost-literature: the Froda ghost-court of the sagas and the writing-spirits of the bishops are one economy - the restless dead's complaints answered by fire in the one and by liturgy in the other.

The bishop's career completes the doctrine: Jon studied abroad (Lincoln and Paris on the record's clauses), reformed the northern see, and exercised the exorcist's office across his diocese - the ghosts of the farms bound by his mass, the saga's miracle-register running from cures to hauntings. And the writing-spirits' resolution completes the episode: the grievance read aloud, the jurisdiction claimed, the spaces consecrated - the haunt ended as a legal proceeding concluded, the conversion-era's dead accepting the church's court. The record thus anchors the church-ghost family: the restless dead's complaints answered by liturgy, distinctive in the written evidence.

Grievance-haunt: the spirits' complaints written in legible letters
Conversion-jurisdiction: the restless dead accepting the church's authority
Bishop-saint portrait: the northern see's holy bishop

title.en: Sunniva and the Seljamenn: Norway's Virgin Martyr of the Cave
title.zh: 桑尼瓦與塞爾雅人：挪威洞穴的殉道貞女

texts.period: Sunnivs saga ok Seljumanna (13th-14th c.); Olafs saga Tryggvasonar en mesta; translatio c. 996; Selja monastery 11th c.

source.work: Sunnivs saga ok Seljumanna; in Olafs saga Tryggvasonar en mesta, ed. Olafur Halldorsson; Flateyjarbok parallel

texts.license: Public domain (older editions); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The Irish princess Sunniva flees the heathen betrothal to Norway's? - to the western isles, lands on Selja, and dies with her company in a cave sealed by a rockslide. King Olaf Tryggvason, guided to the island, opens the cave and finds the bodies incorrupt, sweet-smelling - the Seljamenn - and founds the church; the cave-fragments become Norway's first native relics, and the monastery of Selja (11th c.) the west-coast's cult-center. The record is Norway's oldest native martyr-cycle.
summary.zh: 愛爾蘭公主桑尼瓦為逃避異教婚約而流亡，登陸塞爾雅島，與同伴一同死於被落石封閉的洞穴中。奧拉夫·特里格瓦松王被引導至此，開啟洞穴，發現屍身不朽、散發芬芳——這便是「塞爾雅人」；他隨即建立教堂，洞穴碎石成為挪威最早的本土聖髑，11世紀的塞爾雅修道院則成為西岸崇拜中心。此記錄是挪威最古老的本土殉道傳說。

texts.canonical_translation: Olafs saga Tryggvasonar en mesta, ed. Olafur Halldorsson; paraphrase

narrative.en:
The Sunniva-cycle is Norway's oldest native martyr-cycle, and its structure is the translation-story in reverse: the relics find the king. The flight: Sunniva, an Irish Christian princess, flees a heathen betrothal 'over? - the? - sea? - 'with? - her? - company? - 'and? - 'lands? - on? - Selja? - the island off Sogn; the pursuers? - the? - heathen? - band? - comes? - and? - the? - company? - 'hides? - in? - the? - cave? - 'and? - 'the? - rockslide? - 'seals? - it: the martyrs die sealed in the cave. The finding: Olaf Tryggvason, the conversion-king, is guided to the island (the saga's vision-clause), opens the cave, and finds the bodies incorrupt and sweet-smelling - the Seljamenn - and their incorruption is the proof of sanctity; he founds the church on the spot, and the fragments (the relics of the cave) become Norway's first native relics; the monastery of Selja follows in the 11th century as the west-coast's cult-center.

The record's cultural functions are the incorrupt-relics doctrine and the mission-king's founding doctrine: the conversion-king's authority authenticates the martyr-cult, and the cave-fragments' incorruption is the cult's proof. In the atlas, the record anchors the sealed-martyrs family: each a hidden martyr-company found incorrupt; the Selja one is distinctive in the rockslide and the king's discovery.

The cycle's details document the cult's archaeology: the cave on Selja's south face, the monastery's 11th-century foundation, and the relics' distribution (the Seljamenn's fragments translated to Nidaros and abroad) - Norway's first native relics serving the whole kingdom's church. And the record's literary context is the Olaf Tryggvason-cycle: the conversion-king whose finding of the martyrs authenticates them appears in the same saga-material as the missions and the image-breaking - the mission-king and the martyr-cult as one program. The record thus anchors the north's oldest native sanctity: an Irish princess whose cult made the western isles Norway's holy coast, and whose cave became the mission's own relic-source.

The cult's archaeology completes the doctrine: the cave-chapel on Selja's cliff, the monastery's 11th-century ruins, and the relics' distribution (fragments translated to Nidaros and to the western churches) document the cult's institutional spread - Norway's first native relics serving the kingdom's whole church. And the narrative's structure completes the record: the flight, the sealing, the vision-guided discovery, the king's founding - the translation-story told in reverse, the relics finding the conversion-king rather than the king finding the relics. The record thus anchors the sealed-martyrs family: the hidden company found incorrupt, distinctive in the rockslide and the west-coast cult.

functions: Incorrupt-relics doctrine: the sealed martyrs found sweet-smelling and incorrupt
Mission-king founding: Olaf Tryggvason's authority authenticates the cult
Cave-fragments as first native relics: Norway's own martyr-cycle
Flight-and-sealing narrative structure: the relics find the king
